explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates GPT-4 against human expert evaluations on 100 randomly sampled dialogues with reported agreement metrics and comparison to human inter-annotator agreement

prompts.notes: Evaluation prompts for all 13 tasks shown in appendix Figures 21-34 with detailed scoring guidelines and examples provided

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: human experts agree 80% of the time

guidelines.notes: Human annotators assessed overall quality of multi-turn dialogues based on task requirements using 1-10 scale, with final annotation determined by majority voting

sample_size.notes: 100 randomly sampled dialogues from 4208 total turns across 1388 dialogues

quantitative_scores.notes: GPT-4 vs human experts agreement, compared to human-human agreement of 80%
Appendix Table 9 shows Fleiss' Kappa score confirmed higher agreement between GPT-4 and humans than among humans

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 evaluation achieved 87% agreement with human experts, surpassing the 80% agreement among human experts themselves, validating the effectiveness of their LLM-as-a-judge methodology.

llm_only_criteria: task-specific scoring guidelines for 13 fine-grained abilities
human_only_criteria: overall dialogue quality based on task requirements
criteria_mapping.notes: LLM uses detailed task-specific scoring rubrics while humans assess overall quality, but both evaluate whether responses meet task requirements
